# Weekend, session S1 — wafer-tool-shift

*Generated by `scripts/weekend.py`; every number computed from `runs/` at write time. HEAD `2251bee H77 falsified: the Scratch interaction is on the seen-geometry half`. Long form: `critique_log.md` (numbered entries) and `paper_draft.md`.*

## Read this first

**Identical invocations of one cell do not give the same number, and the spread is larger than most of the effects the Friday tables reported as findings.** Measured by re-running one cell several times per protocol: `iid` 0.0082, `lot` 0.0054, `lot_time` 0.0187, `size` 0.0133. It is not one number — `size` is two and a half times `lot` — and protocols without their own measurement are judged against the largest, because being too strict withdraws a claim and being too lenient publishes one.

**And it does not much matter which of them a comparison is judged against.** Applying every measured floor in turn to every comparison, **22 of 24** give the same verdict whichever is used, and the two that do not are resolved conservatively at their own protocol's floor. No verdict here rests on a borrowed threshold — which is a different question from whether the floors differ, and a more reassuring answer.

**Two standards are used below and it matters which you are reading.** Most tables here hold dozens of cells at three seeds, where a p-value is unavailable at any effect size — an exact permutation test with three per arm has twenty arrangements and a smallest attainable two-sided p of 0.1. Those tables ask whether the seed ranges are disjoint and the margin clears the floor. That is a **screen, not a verdict**: a sample's range grows with the sample, so it becomes stricter as evidence accumulates, and at eight seeds it calls an effect with p = 0.0005 *overlapping*. Where a comparison has been run properly — eight seeds per arm — the permutation test is reported and is the one to believe.

Most of what follows is a withdrawal. Six claims the repository made on Friday do not survive being measured against that floor, and none was withdrawn because a new idea beat an old one. Each closes off a direction that looked open, and two of them — the acquisition cost model and the forward-only decomposition — replace a wrong answer with a better question.

**Two things did come out positive, and both were controlled.** Changing what the encoder pools moved the long tail (section 2.0), and it is the one actionable result here. GroupNorm over BatchNorm survived being re-measured with a test capable of resolving it (section 3).

Nothing here was obtained by loosening a protocol. Where a protocol changed, both numbers are reported and neither is discarded.

## The five-minute version

**One measurement problem underneath everything.** Two identical invocations of one cell differ by more than most effects the Friday tables reported. Three seeds get an effect's sign right and its size wrong, and can get its *existence* wrong in both directions. Four three-seed results here shrank or vanished at eight seeds; one that three seeds called absent is real at p = 0.0003.

**What survived.**

- Replacing the encoder's global average pooling with mean-and-max moves the hardest class (`Scratch`) by +0.0473 on `lot`, p = 0.00047 at 8 seeds, while a capacity control with identical parameter count does not. It holds wherever test wafers share geometry with training and reverses where geometry is held out, which is an artefact of the resize rather than of the method. **The one actionable result.**
- **The borrowed domain-generalization family is worse than ERM**, not merely no better — 8 of 8 seeds negative, exact paired sign-flip p = 0.00781. Dropping the two that are individually significant leaves 8/8 negative at the same p: methods no single test can separate from ERM are jointly worse than it. It replicates on `size`, a different protocol with a different domain vocabulary: 8/8 negative at p = 0.00781, and 7/8 at p = 0.02344 after dropping its one individually significant member.
- GroupNorm beats BatchNorm by +0.0130 on `lot`, p = 0.0106 at 8 seeds per arm — an effect the seed-range screen used elsewhere in this document cannot resolve and never could.

**What was withdrawn, and what it closes off.** Six Friday claims do not survive; none fell because a new idea beat an old one.

- **The RPCA fourth channel helps** — a fourth channel of *zeros* buys the same, and the encoder is handed an intact copy of what the decomposition removed, so it could not have differed. At eight seeds the two are 0.000046 apart, 118 times below the floor, with a test that could have said otherwise. Closes off lot-signature channels for this architecture (§2.3)
- **Lot-adversarial SSL pretraining helps** — worse than random initialisation at every learning rate. Closes off this pretraining objective (§2.3)
- **Active learning loses to random** — it lost while training on a fifth of the labels. At matched *wafer* budget entropy wins at every budget, so the answer depends on whether metrology is priced per lot or per wafer — decision 4 (§2.2)
- **No DG objective is distinguishable from ERM** — replaced by something stronger: the family is significantly *worse* (§2.1)
- **`lot_time` measures temporal drift** — about a quarter of the drop is that its test slice is narrow, and meeting an unseen geometry costs approximately nothing. It measures forward-only deployment (§2.4)
- **Nothing separates from ERM on `size`** — false. At eight seeds `group_dro` (p = 0.0019), `logit_adjust` (p = 0.0050) are worse than ERM; at three the exact test could not return below 0.10 at any effect size. The null was a property of the seed budget (§2.1)
- **The sinkhorn cell's 0.10 macro-F1 is a finding about the method** — it is a badly chosen weight — one of the four questions handed over. At the default lambda = 1.0 the model collapses to one class; with the penalty off it lands 0.0009 from the nearest ERM seed, inside the floor, so the code is sound. No lambda beats zero, so there is no operating point (§2.3a)
- **An arm scattering wider than its effect is unstable, not worse** — our own criterion, and wrong. At eight seeds all six `size` arms still scatter wider than their effect and `group_dro` separates anyway — a difference of means is estimated far more precisely than a single draw (§2.1)

**What needs a human.** Four decisions with options are in section 4. Only one blocks work: whether metrology is priced per lot or per wafer, because the two answers reverse the active-learning conclusion and nobody here can settle it.

**Still running.** Nothing; all stages complete.

## 2.0 The one thing that worked: what the encoder pools


| pooling | macro-F1 | vs `mean` | verdict | Scratch F1 | vs `mean` | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mean` — global average, the original | 0.8738 (n=8) | — | — | 0.7292 | — | — |
| `meanmax` — **treatment** | 0.8888 (n=8) | +0.0150 | overlaps | 0.7764 | +0.0473 | overlaps |
| `meanmean` — **capacity control** | 0.8793 (n=8) | +0.0055 | overlaps | 0.7354 | +0.0063 | overlaps |

**Ignore the `verdict` columns above and read this table instead.** Those verdicts ask whether the seed ranges overlap, which is the right default for a table of three-seed cells and the wrong tool once a comparison has been run properly — a sample's range grows with the sample, so more seeds make non-overlap strictly harder. An exact permutation test does not punish extra data:

| metric | seeds/arm | difference | range test | exact permutation p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| macro-F1 | 8 | +0.0150 | ranges overlap | **0.01197** |
| Scratch F1 | 8 | +0.0473 | ranges overlap | **0.00047** |

The effect is concentrated in `Scratch`, at a p more than twenty times smaller than macro-F1's — which is what the mechanism predicts, and it was predicted before the run rather than observed after it. The range test calling this *overlaps* at p = 0.0005 is the clearest illustration in this repository of why the criterion used elsewhere is a floor and not a verdict.

**Across all four protocols, eight seeds per arm.** This is the shape of the finding and it is not the macro-F1 row:

| protocol | metric | vs `mean` | exact permutation p |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iid` | Scratch | +0.0389 | **0.00093** |
| `iid` | macro-F1 | +0.0113 | **0.00031** |
| `lot` | Scratch | +0.0473 | **0.00047** |
| `lot` | macro-F1 | +0.0150 | **0.01197** |
| `lot_time` | Scratch | +0.0391 | **0.00031** |
| `lot_time` | macro-F1 | +0.0038 | **0.43046** |
| `size` | Scratch | -0.0427 | **0.20233** |
| `size` | macro-F1 | -0.0281 | **0.16177** |

`Scratch` improves on **every protocol where the test wafers share their geometry with training** — `iid` at 99.95% shared, `lot` at 99.7%, `lot_time` at 86% — each at p ≤ 0.001, and it fails only on `size`, which holds geometry out entirely. macro-F1 follows where one class can move a nine-class average and does not on `lot_time`, where it cannot. A max over a resampled feature map depends on the die density of the wafer it came from, so the statistic that recovers a thin structure is the one that does not transfer across geometry.

**That mechanism was a story told after the fact, so it was tested on its own, with no model involved.** `resize_nearest` upsamples by indexing and 97.7% of wafers are upsampled, so a one-die scratch arrives as a band about 64/w pixels wide — a width set by native geometry. Over four oriented line filters on the 577 `Scratch` wafers in the 11 geometries with at least 30 each, failure fraction removed, geometry explains **77%** of the max-pooled response and 15% of the mean-pooled one. Run again at *native* resolution, where a one-die scratch is one die wide on every geometry, the max-pooled figure collapses to 0.0629. **The resize creates the geometry dependence; it is not a property of the wafers** — and so the one thing that worked is not inherently geometry-bound.

**The repair I wrote down first was wrong, and one script said so before any GPU time was spent.** Pooling the response back onto the native die grid before the max — the obvious way to undo a 64/w replication — leaves η² at 0.7511, essentially uncorrected, because convolution and downsampling do not commute. Dilating the *filter* by round(64/w) instead gives **0.0361**. The fix is a scale-aware receptive field, not scale-aware pooling.

**We then built it, and it failed badly — which is the most useful negative of the weekend.** An encoder whose first block dilates by round(64/w) loses 0.1758 of `Scratch` F1 on `lot` (p = 0.00016) and 0.1094 on `size` (p = 0.01523) against plain `meanmax`, at eight seeds per arm. It is worse than the thing it was meant to rescue. The implementation is not the excuse: it adds no parameters, is bit-exact with the unscaled path at w = 64, and matches a per-sample reference to 7.5e-09.

The measurement stands and the remedy does not. The resize really does make a defect's apparent width a function of geometry; we have not shown that is *removable*.

**H69 asked which half was at fault, and the answer keeps the mechanism alive while leaving the lever dead.** Dilating the first block by a *constant* 2 — the value 77.9% of wafers receive — is worse than plain `meanmax` by 0.2844 on `Scratch` (p = 0.00016), so dilation itself is the problem and H66's failure says nothing about whether the geometry confound is real. But the geometry-adaptive version beats the fixed one by 0.1087 on `Scratch` (p = 0.00808) and not on macro-F1 (p = 0.44227) — the thin-structure-only pattern the mechanism predicts. Consistent with it, not confirmation: both arms are far worse than doing nothing, and a difference between two broken configurations is weak evidence about a good one.

`CnnResized.embed` was a global average over the final feature map. A `Scratch` is a thin connected line; averaged over the wafer it is close to a slightly elevated background failure rate, which is exactly the statistic that discards the fact that the failures form a line. Concatenating a max recovers it.

**`meanmean` is why this is a result and not a number.** It has `meanmax`'s exact parameter count and carries the mean concatenated with itself, so it separates "max pooling helps" from "a wider head helps". It buys nothing. The RPCA channel died on precisely this question, asked after the fact; here it was asked first.

Three other explanations for the long tail were measured and discarded first: focal loss over five values of gamma against its own bit-exact `gamma = 0` control, class-balanced weighting, and input resolution — the last refuted outright, since 97.7% of wafers are *upsampled* to reach 64x64 and a finer grid has nothing to recover. **The long tail was an architecture problem, not a class-imbalance problem.** That is the sentence worth taking away.

*Caveat, resolved. This began as a single-protocol win on `lot` with the note that the other three were still running. They have since finished and are in the table above, and the caveat was half right: the effect replicates on `iid` and `lot_time` and is not established on `size` (p = 0.20233). The claim is therefore conditional on geometry being represented in training, which is stated as the finding rather than as a limitation. It is no longer one encoder: repeated on `cnn_bn`, which differs in the normalisation layer alone, `meanmax` beats `mean` on `Scratch` by +0.0322 (p = 0.01010) while the capacity control stays null (p = 0.25781). The gain is not a property of GroupNorm.*

## 2. What was withdrawn, and what each withdrawal rules out

### 2.1 "No borrowed DG objective beats ERM" — the experiment could not have shown otherwise, and the conclusion survives anyway

Every group-aware objective was handed `lot % 32` as its domain: 10,762 lots averaged into 32 buckets. Mean pairwise label total-variation between those buckets is **0.0208**, against 0.1666 between real lots and 0.1822 between production-order deciles. An invariance penalty asked to equalize distributions that are already equal is satisfied by doing nothing.

Re-run against production deciles — nine times the label shift — with every objective compared to ERM measured under the *same* domain definition:

| objective | macro-F1 | vs ERM | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `coral` | 0.8493 ±0.0131 (n=8) | -0.0092 | overlaps |
| `dann` | 0.8487 ±0.0154 (n=8) | -0.0098 | overlaps |
| `group_dro` | 0.8384 ±0.0200 (n=8) | -0.0201 | overlaps |
| `hsic` | 0.8556 ±0.0160 (n=8) | -0.0029 | overlaps |
| `irm` | 0.8539 ±0.0120 (n=8) | -0.0045 | overlaps |
| `mixup_domain` | 0.8405 ±0.0168 (n=8) | -0.0180 | overlaps |

**None of them beats ERM.** So the original claim was unearned and its direction was right: the experiment as run could not have shown otherwise, and the corrected experiment agrees that nothing helps.

**But "nothing is distinguishable from ERM" was wrong, and it was wrong because three seeds cannot see it.** All six objectives are now at eight seeds per arm, read with an exact permutation test against ERM at the same seeds:

| objective | seeds/arm | vs ERM | exact permutation p | Holm-adjusted p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `group_dro` | 8 | -0.0201 | **0.00171** | **0.0103** |
| `mixup_domain` | 8 | -0.0180 | **0.00513** | **0.0256** |
| `dann` | 8 | -0.0098 | 0.07770 | 0.3108 |
| `coral` | 8 | -0.0092 | 0.08718 | 0.3108 |
| `irm` | 8 | -0.0045 | 0.33800 | 0.6760 |
| `hsic` | 8 | -0.0029 | 0.58073 | 0.6760 |

**Every one of the six is negative.** 2 reach p < 0.05 individually and 2 survive Holm-Bonferroni over the six tests — which has to be shown rather than asserted, because reporting two significant results out of six without saying six were run is the oldest way to manufacture a finding.

**The six all pointing the same way is itself a result, and the obvious way to test it is wrong.** The comparisons share one ERM baseline and one corpus, so they are not independent and a sign test across objectives would badly overstate its evidence. Pairing by seed avoids that: a seed fixes the split, the initialisation and the batch order, so the mean of the six objectives minus ERM *at the same seed* gives 8 paired differences that can be sign-flipped exactly.

All 8 of 8 are negative, mean -0.0107, **p = 0.00781** over 256 sign assignments. **The borrowed objective family as a whole is worse than ERM on this corpus.**

**And it is not the two significant ones carrying the other four.** Drop `group_dro` and `mixup_domain` entirely and repeat the test on the four that individually fail to separate from ERM — `coral`, `dann`, `irm`, `hsic` — and it still gives 8 of 8 seeds negative at **p = 0.00781**, mean -0.0066. Every one of the six leave-one-out subsets does the same. **Four methods that no individual test can distinguish from ERM are, together, clearly worse than it** — which is the cleanest statement of this benchmark's thesis that the repository contains.

That p is the floor of this test — with 8 seeds, 256 sign assignments, nothing below 0.00781 is reachable. The result is as strong as eight seeds can make it and no stronger; a smaller p would need more seeds, not a better argument.

The corrected claim is that none of the borrowed objectives helps, the family is established as harmful in aggregate, and two objectives are individually harmful after correction for multiplicity. That is a better result than the null it replaces: a uniformly null table cannot show that the benchmark would detect a harmful method if one existed, and this does. **Rules out:** this family of invariance objectives on this corpus, now with evidence rather than with silence.

**And the `size` protocol, which was the half of this result said to 'stand', does not stand either.** It was the only place a borrowed objective showed a large effect, and those cells were single-seed. Re-run at three seeds in one session, with `size`'s own run-to-run floor measured first (0.0133, two and a half times `lot`'s):

| objective | vs ERM on `size` | its own seed range | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group_dro` | -0.1291 | 0.2220 | overlaps |
| `logit_adjust` | -0.0887 | 0.1387 | overlaps |

**At 8 seeds per arm it resolves, and it resolves against the objectives.** `group_dro` (-0.1291, p = 0.0019), `logit_adjust` (-0.0887, p = 0.0050) — worse than ERM, at effects several times anything measured on `lot`. At three seeds the exact test could not return below 0.10 at any effect size; at 8 its floor is 0.0002. The earlier null was a property of the seed budget, not of the methods.

**And a criterion this document proposed has to be withdrawn.** At three seeds all 6 arms had a seed range wider than their own distance from ERM, and we wrote that an arm scattering further than it has moved is *unstable* rather than worse. That is wrong. At 8 seeds all 6 still scatter wider than their effect — `group_dro` spans 0.2220 while sitting 0.1291 below ERM — and it separates anyway at p = 0.0019. A difference of means is estimated far more precisely than a single draw. It is the range-overlap error again, made by us, one section after diagnosing it.

*The RPCA channel was also re-tested on `lot_time`, the one protocol where a real tool signature should help, since lots there are ordered in production time. At eight seeds the residual leads a channel of zeros by +0.00288 (p = 0.4656). The earlier three-seed observation that it led at every seed was three of three, which a coin gives a quarter of the time.*

**Rules out:** this family of invariance objectives on this corpus, on both protocols — negatively established on `lot` in aggregate and on `size` for two objectives individually, rather than merely unobserved.

### 2.2 "Active learning lost to random" — it lost while training on a fifth of the data

| at a 400-lot budget | wafers labelled | wafers per lot | share of random's |
|---|---|---|---|
| random | 6,284 | 15.71 | 100.0% |
| entropy | 1,104 | 2.76 | 17.6% |
| coreset | 1,820 | 4.55 | 29.0% |
| diverse | 1,344 | 3.36 | 21.4% |

The budget was counted in lots. A lot's acquisition score is the *mean* of its wafers' scores, and the maximum of noisy means favours small samples, so "take the top-scoring lots" is substantially "take the smallest lots".

Re-run with the budget in **wafers**, so every strategy stops at the same supervision volume:

| macro-F1 | 400 wafers | 800 wafers | 1,600 wafers | 3,200 wafers | 6,400 wafers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| random | 0.4274 | 0.4923 | 0.5942 | 0.6697 | 0.7257 |
| entropy | 0.5456 | 0.5954 | 0.7003 | 0.7432 | 0.7770 |
| coreset | 0.5539 | 0.5904 | 0.6642 | 0.7151 | 0.7681 |
| diverse | 0.5010 | 0.5610 | 0.6332 | 0.7364 | 0.7434 |

| lots it took | 400 | 800 | 1,600 | 3,200 | 6,400 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| random | 25 | 54 | 103 | 205 | 397 |
| entropy | 95 | 365 | 666 | 1,008 | 1,355 |
| coreset | 92 | 355 | 557 | 957 | 1,653 |
| diverse | 47 | 204 | 514 | 941 | 1,293 |

The ranking reverses: entropy reaches 0.7770 against random's 0.7257 at 6,400 wafers, and leads at every budget. **But it needs 3.4x the metrology slots for the same measured wafers.** Neither result is a fact about active learning; both are facts about active learning plus a cost model that was never stated. **Rules out:** reporting either curve alone. See Decision 4.

### 2.3a The sinkhorn cell — one of the four questions handed over

Friday reported a sinkhorn cell at macro-F1 0.1026 and read it as a property of the method. The brief asked for a lambda sweep and for the claim to be removed if it was still broken. Sweeping the transport weight on `lot`/`cnn_bn`:

| transport weight λ | macro-F1 | Scratch F1 |  |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0 | 0.8609 | 0.7224 |  |
| 0.003 | 0.8591 | 0.6992 |  |
| 0.01 | 0.8540 | 0.7037 |  |
| 0.03 | 0.8573 | 0.7120 |  |
| 0.1 | 0.8485 | 0.6921 |  |
| 0.3 | 0.8352 | 0.6798 |  |
| 1.0 | 0.1026 | 0.0000 | **collapses to one class** |

**The control is the λ = 0 row, and it is what makes this a diagnosis rather than an observation.** With the penalty weighted to zero the objective is plain cross-entropy, so the cell has to land where ERM lands — and it does, 0.8609 against ERM's 0.8448–0.8600 over 6 seeds on the same cell, 0.0009 from the nearest. That is inside the run-to-run floor. **The collapse is the weight, not a broken implementation** — which is the difference between "this method fails here" and "we ran it wrong", and Friday's table asserted the first.

**And there is no operating point.** macro-F1 falls monotonically as λ rises and the best value in the sweep is λ = 0, which is ERM with extra machinery. The claim is withdrawn: not because the method was refuted, but because the number that stood for it was measuring a hyperparameter.

*Limit, and it is the usual one: 1 seed per λ. The ordering among the non-collapsed rows is not established — their whole spread is comparable to ERM's own seed range of 0.0151. What the sweep establishes is the shape and the two endpoints, and those do not need seeds: the drop to 0.1026 is 50 times ERM's own seed range on this cell.*

### 2.3 Our own two contributions, and one of our own metrics

**The RPCA lot-signature channel.** Its low-rank part is rank 0 for 94.8% of decomposed wafers and the residual it hands the encoder is bit-identical to the raw failed-die mask for 95.3% of all wafers. On `lot`:

| fourth channel | macro-F1 | vs 3-channel | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| RPCA residual (the claim) | 0.8696 ±0.0096 (n=3) | +0.0049 | overlaps |
| raw failed-die mask | 0.8692 ±0.0065 (n=3) | +0.0045 | overlaps |
| **zeros** | 0.8689 ±0.0075 (n=3) | +0.0042 | overlaps |
| no fourth channel | 0.8647 ±0.0044 (n=3) | — | — |

A channel of **zeros** buys what the decomposition buys. **Rules out:** per-lot RPCA as a domain normalization here — lots do not share enough for it to have anything to remove.

**Lot-adversarial SSL pretraining** on 638,506 unlabelled wafers:

| protocol | from scratch | SSL-initialized | delta | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lot` | 0.8647 ±0.0044 (n=3) | 0.8143 ±0.0091 (n=3) | -0.0504 | **clears the floor** |
| `size` | 0.8467 ±0.0346 (n=3) | 0.7711 ±0.0265 (n=3) | -0.0756 | below the floor (0.0173 < 0.0187) |
| `lot_time` | 0.6985 ±0.0045 (n=3) | 0.6345 ±0.0225 (n=3) | -0.0640 | **clears the floor** |

The obvious confound — that the fine-tuning recipe was tuned for a random init — is refuted, and in the predicted direction. Sweeping both arms over learning rates, the gap *widens* as the rate falls (2e-4: -0.1464; 5e-4: -0.1102; 1e-3: -0.0935), where a recipe mismatch predicts it closing. **Rules out:** this masked-die plus gradient-reversal recipe.

**Our own `p10 domain F1` metric cannot rank models.** 67 separate `lot` cells report the identical value 0.489796, and the whole set of 105 cells takes only 11 distinct values. A lot holds at most 25 wafers, so a lot whose single defect is missed scores exactly (48/49 + 0)/2 whichever model missed it. The metric meant to stop a model hiding a bad tool behind a good average could not separate any two models. **Rules out:** per-lot worst-group statistics on domains this small.

### 2.4 The forward-only result is a compound, and a quarter of it is not time

| protocol | geometries in train | in test | test wafers of unseen geometry |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iid` | 327 | 266 | 0.05% |
| `lot` | 320 | 209 | 0.28% |
| `size` | 205 | 139 | 100.00% |
| `lot_time` | 338 | 19 | 14.15% |

`lot_time` tests on a narrow geometry slice. To see whether that slice is *intrinsically* hard, score the **`iid`** models — random split, every one of those geometries seen in training, no temporal structure — on their own test wafers restricted to it:

| representation | full test (matched classes) | restricted to those geometries | cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| cnn_bn | 0.8623 | 0.8040 | -0.0583 |
| cnn_gn | 0.8820 | 0.8356 | -0.0464 |
| feat | 0.8532 | 0.7673 | -0.0859 |
| spectral | 0.8578 | 0.7872 | -0.0706 |

Several points, with no time and no unseen geometry involved — many times the floor. The full `iid`-to-`lot_time` drop is about 0.18, so **roughly a quarter of it is the test set being narrow.** **Rules out:** reading `lot_time` as a measurement of temporal drift. It measures forward-only *deployment*, of which drift is one part.

### 2.5 One thing checked and *not* withdrawn

Both external reviewers flagged that the group splits read candidate groups' labels. Dropping the guard entirely and comparing the partitions: it fired in 0/10 seeds on `lot`, 0/10 seeds on `size`, and the partitions are identical wafer for wafer. Structurally so — the guard rejects a group only if it holds *all* remaining training examples of a class, and no lot holds more than 4.14% of any class. The code path is label-aware; the split is not. This was in last revision's decision list on the strength of two reviewers agreeing; four minutes of CPU settled it.

## 3. What survives the floor

| finding | size |
|---|---|
| **Max pooling beats global average pooling** | +0.0150 macro-F1 and +0.0473 on `Scratch`; the capacity control gives +0.0055 and +0.0063, neither significant at eight seeds |
| **The pooling gain is not extra parameters** | the capacity control at eight seeds gives +0.0063 on class:Scratch (p = 0.591) and +0.0055 on macro_f1 (p = 0.360) |
| **Two DG objectives are worse than ERM** | `group_dro` -0.0201 (p = 0.0017), `mixup_domain` -0.0180 (p = 0.0051), `coral` -0.0092 (p = 0.0872), `dann` -0.0098 (p = 0.0777), `irm` -0.0045 (p = 0.3380), `hsic` -0.0029 (p = 0.5807), at eight seeds under real domains |
| **GroupNorm beats BatchNorm** | +0.0130 on `lot`, permutation p = 0.0106 over 8 seeds per arm — the range test cannot resolve it and never could |
| The RPCA residual is a worse description of the defect than the raw mask | -0.0271 when it is the *only* description; indistinguishable when the raw mask is also present |
| SSL init is worse than random init | -0.0504 on `lot`, and at every learning rate |
| The die-graph GNN is last | -0.0860 against the next-worst representation on `lot` |
| The forward-only geometry slice is intrinsically hard | -0.0859 to -0.0464 on `iid`, where nothing else differs |
| Acquisition beats random at matched wafer budget | +0.0512 at 6,400 wafers, at 3.4x the metrology slots |

Everything else this repository reported is inside the floor, inside the seed spread, or has no error bar at all.

## 4. Four things that need a human decision

**Decision 1 — MixedWM38, or drop the multi-label target.** WM-811K is single-label, so "multi-label F1" is not defined on it. MixedWM38 could not be acquired from this machine: the HuggingFace copy (`wafervqaanon/MixedWM38-VQA`) is gated behind manual approval and Zenodo `10.5281/zenodo.20061545` returns HTTP 403 on its files. Options: **(a)** supply Kaggle credentials or request the gated copy — one human action, and the number becomes measurable on the real benchmark; **(b)** accept **MIXED-SYNTH**, built this weekend from overlaid WM-811K patterns, lot-disjoint, labelled synthetic everywhere, and report it as an upper bound; **(c)** drop the target as not well posed here. *Recommendation: (a) if anyone can spare five minutes, else (b) with the upper-bound caveat kept in front.*

**Decision 2 — what to do about the 0.95 target, now that it is measured.** Measured: 0.8427 on the optimistic split and 0.8177 lot-disjoint, both on MIXED-SYNTH, which is an upper bound on the real task. The shortfall is 0.1073 at best. Focal's seed range overlaps plain BCE's on both protocols, so the loss named in the target contributes nothing. Options: **(a)** keep the honest lot-disjoint number as the headline and make the gap to the optimistic protocol the contribution; **(b)** chase 0.95 on an iid split with augmentation and a bigger backbone, reported clearly as the optimistic protocol. *Recommendation: (a). The gap is the paper. Closing it by loosening the split is the one thing these rules forbid, and the levers that remain — backbone, pooling, real mixed-type data — are not tuning.*

**Decision 3 — how should the forward-only result be framed?** It is the largest number here and section 2.4 shows it is a compound: a quarter of it is that the test slice is intrinsically hard, and the rest is drift. The geometry share is now measured and is not a share: over 15 cells whose seen and unseen halves contain the same classes, unseen-geometry macro-F1 differs from seen-geometry macro-F1 by -0.0077 on average and +0.0010 at the median, with 6 of 15 cells negative — it straddles zero. Meeting a geometry never trained on, which we assumed was the expensive part, costs approximately nothing; the expensive part is that the slice is narrow. (22 further cells are excluded because the two halves contain different classes and macro-F1 over eight is not comparable to macro-F1 over nine.) Options: **(a)** reframe as *forward-only deployment* — a fab does meet new products going forward, so the geometry shift is part of the phenomenon rather than a confound; **(b)** build a geometry-controlled temporal protocol, isolating drift but measuring something no fab experiences; **(c)** report both. *Recommendation: (a) with the decomposition printed beside it. A fab does not get to hold its product mix fixed.*

**Decision 4 — which acquisition cost model is real?** This is the one question here that only someone who knows the metrology contract can answer, and the two answers point opposite ways. Priced per **lot**, random acquisition wins and the heuristics waste slots on near-empty lots. Priced per **wafer measured**, entropy wins at every budget. *Recommendation: state the fab's actual cost model; both curves are already measured and reported.*

## 5. What is running, and how to check it

```
tail -f logs/chain_s1.log            # stage transitions
nvidia-smi                           # devices 0,1 only; 2,3 are another loop's
ls -t runs/*.json | head             # newest cells
python scripts/report.py && python scripts/paper.py && python scripts/weekend.py
python scripts/check_all.py          # <- run this one; it runs the rest
python scripts/section_diff.py --accept   # after an intended section change
python tests/run_tests.py            # no pytest in the shared pdeno env, by design
python scripts/guard_audit.py        # do the checks themselves catch anything?
```

| stage | status | log | what it decides |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repr_one_session.sh` | done | `logs/repr_one_session.log` | 66 cells: every (protocol, representation) pair at three seeds, all in one session, because mixing Friday's seed 0 with this weekend's seeds 1-2 folds a session offset into what is presented as seed variance. Reported beside the original table, not replacing it |
| `pooling_sweep.sh` | done | `logs/pooling.log` | **answered** (section 2.0): max pooling beats global average pooling on `lot` and the capacity control does not |
| `size_objectives_seeds.sh` | done | `logs/size_objectives.log` | **superseded** — it reported that nothing separates from ERM on `size`, which the instrument could not have shown: three seeds per arm bottom out at p = 0.10. See `size_complete.sh` |
| `gn_vs_bn.sh` | done | `logs/gn_vs_bn.log` | **answered**: GroupNorm beats BatchNorm, permutation p = 0.011 at eight seeds per arm |
| `rpca_ablation_clean.sh` | done | `logs/rpca_clean.log` | **answered**: all four fourth-channel arms within the floor of each other, as the original ablation said |
| `rpca_hide_raw.sh` | done | `logs/rpca_hide_raw.log` | **answered on the second attempt**; the first was void because the one-hot planes sum to 1 and the 'hidden' plane was recoverable |
| `pooling_protocols.sh` | done | `logs/pooling_protocols.log` | **answered** (section 2.0): the win holds on `iid`, `lot` and `lot_time` at p <= 0.001 on `Scratch` and reverses on `size`. The prediction on record was half right — it holds on `iid` and does *not* shrink on `lot_time`; what breaks it is geometry holdout, not forward-only shift |
| `dg_complete.sh` | done | `logs/dg_complete.log` | **answered** (section 2.1): all six borrowed objectives at eight seeds. The family is worse than ERM in aggregate, exact sign-flip p = 0.00781; two survive Holm correction individually |
| `size_complete.sh` | done | `logs/size_complete.log` | the seven `size` arms to eight seeds, because at three the exact test cannot return anything below 0.10 and every arm's own seed range is wider than its effect. Decides whether `size` is negative or merely unresolved. **H64 on record** — `group_dro` and `logit_adjust` separate; `coral`, `dann`, `irm`, `mixup_domain` do not |
| `scale_aware_sweep.sh` | done | `logs/scale_aware.log` | 16 cells testing whether a receptive field dilated by round(64/w) recovers the pooling gain on `size`. Measured with no model: the resize makes a defect's apparent width a function of geometry, and dilating the filter removes that. **H66 on record** — it beats plain `meanmax` on `size` `Scratch` and turns the effect against `mean` positive; little change on `lot` |

### Our own track record on our own predictions

Every sweep here states a prediction in its header before it launches, and each is scored afterwards with an explicit verdict in `state/hypothesis_outcomes.json`. Of 19 scored: **10 held as stated**, 4 were partly right — usually direction correct, threshold wrong — and 5 failed outright, with 1 still running.

That is a little over half, and it is the number to weigh anything here by. A record showing near-perfect foresight would mean the predictions were written to be safe or written after the fact. `python scripts/hypothesis_ledger.py` fails if a sweep has finished and its prediction was never given a verdict, which is the one way a record like this quietly becomes a list of successes.

### Which of these checks are evidence, and which are not

Every guard in `scripts/` is fed a defect it claims to catch, by `python scripts/guard_audit.py`. The defects are the ones this repository actually shipped — a stage producing three cells where eight were launched, a section body left inside its own input loop, an input referenced through a tuple, two arms disjoint by less than the run-to-run floor. A guard that passes its own broken input is reported as **VACUOUS**, which is worse than a failing one: it means every green result it has produced was uninformative.

`python scripts/check_all.py` runs all six checks and prints one verdict with one exit code. That exists because reading six separate outputs is how a failing check got past this loop: the ratchet below was red, a fix was applied, it stayed red, and the commit went in anyway because the line that was read came from the patch script rather than the guard. If you inherit this, run the one command.

**One of these was added because the others could not see it.** A section of `paper_draft.md` disappeared silently when its guard turned out to be conditioned on a problem existing and the problem was fixed — and every check passed on the shorter paper, because they all reason about inputs and generator source rather than about the rendered document. `section_diff.py` compares each document's headings against the last accepted shape and fails when one is removed. Growth never fails; a deliberate removal is recorded with `--accept`, which leaves a diff in git rather than silence.

Run it before trusting anything below. One check is currently vacuous by construction and says so: `number_provenance.py`'s traceability half accepts most random four-digit decimals, because `runs/` holds tens of thousands of values and almost any number matches one. Its ratchet half — the count of decimals typed into generator prose, which may only go down — does fail when it should.

### A property of this codebase worth knowing before you run anything

**Its default failure mode is silence.** Four times this weekend a stage logged completion having produced nothing, or less than it claimed, and every one was found by an incidental check rather than by anything failing:

| what happened | what it looked like |
|---|---|
| `sweep_c.sh` built a log path containing a `/` from `--init-from runs/ssl_pretrain.pt` | bash failed the redirect before exec; three SSL cells never ran while the sweep logged "launch" for each |
| `report.py` keyed cells without the seed | a second seed of any cell would have silently replaced the first |
| the first wafer-budget acquisition run was OOM-killed | its stage printed `=== al wafer budget done ===` and wrote no JSON |
| `pooling_size_seeds.sh` invoked the permutation test with globs hardcoded to another protocol | zero files matched; it printed a note and returned 0 |

The shared shape is that **a stage boundary converts an error into an absence**, and an absence is invisible unless something counts. `scripts/verify_stage.py` is that counter — a glob and an integer, deliberately dumb, because a check that is hard to add does not get added. It is wired into the stages that end by writing a summary file, which is where three of the four failures landed. **Any new sweep should end with it.**

The corollary for reading anything here: a missing result is not a null result. If a table says [not measured], check whether the run happened before concluding the effect is zero.

The metric backfill (`scripts/backfill_metrics.sh`) is **deliberately blocked** and should stay blocked: it refuses to overwrite measured cells while a fresh re-run does not reproduce them, and overwriting the Friday cells would destroy the only record of the session offset in section 1 — which is now one of the more useful things this repository knows about itself.

Nothing wrote outside this repository, nothing touched GPUs 2 or 3, and no package was installed into any shared environment. `runs.bak_*/` is Friday's `runs/` verbatim, gitignored, kept so any re-run can be checked against what it replaced.
